items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: in the setting of the punctual topos with a cosimplicial object as in the resolution lemma, a flat B-module F with H_0(C, F) = 0 satisfies H_l(C, Sym^k(F)) = 0 for l < k (source lines 2281-2292). The proof is an induction on k built on the Koszul-type exact complex whose terms are wedge powers tensored with symmetric powers: viewing it as a resolution of Sym^k(F) produces a first quadrant spectral sequence converging to the homology of Sym^k(F), the Eilenberg-Zilber lemma rewrites the derived lower shriek of each term as a derived tensor product of two derived lower shrieks, and the induction hypothesis together with the vanishing of H_0 of the wedge powers (a quotient of F^{tensor q+1}) gives the claim.
